info.title: Envai AaaS API: execution plane and control plane
info.description:
Contract for the Envai AaaS HTTP surface covering both the execution plane and the control plane. The execution plane serves the Agent Team Protocol (ATP) through the Go gateway: the caller sends messages to a chat, steers or cancels the active turn through small control endpoints, restores a chat from client held context, and reads every agent's activity from one multiplexed SSE stream which is the single source of truth. The chat is the only execution entity: one chat holds one history and hosts many turns, and no parallel run or session lifecycle exists beside it. All endpoints live under the canonical `/api/v1` prefix; legacy `/v1` paths are not aliases and receive no redirect. Event envelopes and per-type payloads are defined once in `events.json` and referenced by the events endpoint through external `$ref`.
The control plane surface served by Laravel is in scope here: workspaces, chats, completion metadata, agent definitions, teams, models, api keys, image operations, signed artifacts and provider webhooks. Control plane responses use the Laravel JsonResource `{data: ...}` wrapper for single resources and collections, except the provider webhook which answers a bare `{status: ok}` and the model catalogs which answer a top-level `{object, data, defaults}` object. Since 1.1.0 the image operations are reserved to authenticated api keys. Since 1.2.0 the workspace files api exposes the workspace fake filesystem (wiki, skills and `MEMORY.md` are plain files under it) through the control plane.
 Contract3 is selected with X-Envai-Contract-Version: 3. Canonical execution routes include /atp/v3 and never downgrade. Old execution mutation routes return 426. Legacy event reads are finite historical snapshots, not live subscriptions. Successful negotiated responses acknowledge the selected version; clients must validate before hydration.

servers.description: Local development edge (control plane single entrypoint)

post.description: Authenticated native system input. Idle chats wake in a new turn. Busy chats queue until the active turn terminates. Identical event_id retries return the same receipt with duplicate=true; changed content returns 409. Origin turn must be known to this live chat. Receipts and deduplication are process-local and may be lost on restart or eviction. Never blindly retry an uncertain paid operation after state loss.

400.description: Malformed JSON or unsupported contract version

404.description: Chat or task is missing or outside the authenticated scope

409.description: Conflicting idempotency key or active target turn

post.description: Workflow consumers must require the delegated_job_lifecycle capability before relying on complete-job terminal semantics. Origin and target chats must belong to the authenticated owner and the same workspace. Target team is resolved from its existing chat binding. Execution and completion delivery are native Envai operations; the origin turn can finish independently. task_id identifies the complete delegated job; receipt turn_id identifies only its initial target coordinator turn. If that turn delegates detached children, its terminal does not complete the job. Envai waits for the coordinator terminal and all pending children in each cohort, then batches their results into one target synthesis turn. A synthesis that delegates more children starts another cohort. Only a coordinator turn with no pending children or results finalizes the origin task and its integral output. Use origin task.completed or origin GET task terminal status as the phase outcome. Task output is the full final job output, and optional result_turn_id identifies its final coordinator turn. A new delegation whose origin_turn_id belongs to a delegated job can attach only to its currently active coordinator turn; a past coordinator turn is rejected with 422. Exact duplicates still replay their receipt. Keep target-chat SSE open through job terminal for tools and submit their results to that target chat; tool events are not forwarded to origin. Optional notify_origin defaults to true. With the delegation_notify_origin capability, false suppresses only automatic origin delivery and model wake; origin task events, GET, final output and result_turn_id remain available, and target child cohorts and synthesis are unchanged. Omitted and explicit true are equivalent for idempotency; changing the effective boolean for the same event_id returns 409. Optional strict_model defaults to false; true rejects an unavailable configured target root model before admission with 422 strict_model_unavailable and persists the policy through coordinator synthesis turns. Root agent.started.model reports the requested selection; agent.done.requested_model identifies that selection and optional agent.done.model preserves the last provider-reported model, including aliases. An active target chat returns 409. Deduplication is process-local.

post.summary: Send a message and start a turn
post.description: Sends a user message to the chat. The message opens a turn: the gateway resolves the team from `chat.team_id` and starts the orchestrator loop, and the turn is identified by the orchestrator completion id `cmpl_<ulid>` returned as `turn_id`. The server emits `turn.started` with the message as the turn input. The request is rejected with 409 when a turn is already in progress for the chat, with 503 `server_error`/`gateway_draining` while the gateway is draining, and with 404 when the chat does not exist.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Required with attachment_ids; reuse on deliberate retry to recover the same accepted turn.

409.description: A turn is already in progress for this chat

error.message: A turn is already in progress for this chat.

get.description: Server-Sent Events stream with one `data:` line per event, JSON encoded. Attach with `after=<seq>` to receive retained events strictly after that sequence number. In the current implementation the replay window is bounded and in memory; eviction or restart discards events, resets sequence to 1 and exposes no epoch or cursor-expired signal. Within a resident runtime, positive sequence numbers are monotonic and continuous across turns, including chat.extension placeholders for extension-only events. A wire-only `ping` with `seq: 0` is emitted periodically to keep proxies and load balancers from closing the idle stream. Each `data:` line is one Agent Team Protocol event envelope; `type` discriminates `data`, and the envelope and every per-type payload are defined in `events.json`.

Cache-Control.description: Streams must not be buffered by proxies

X-Envai-Extensions.description: Present only when native-tasks-v1 was accepted

schema.description: SSE frames whose `data` field contains one ATP event envelope

post.description: Stops the active turn and emits `turn.cancelled`. In flight subagents are cancelled through context propagation. The request is rejected with 409 when no turn is in progress for the chat.

409.description: No turn is in progress for this chat

error.message: No turn is in progress for this chat.

post.summary: Record guidance for the active turn
post.description: Validates that a turn is active and records guidance by echoing `turn.steered`. `target_agent_id` is optional and targets the orchestrator when omitted. In the current alpha implementation the text is not injected into the running LLM loop.

Resolves a client tool call (`agent.tool.request`) with the client output. The body carries `call_id` and `output` (required; `output` is the double-encoded JSON string of the client tool contract) and `is_error` (optional, default false). Resolution is at most once by `call_id` while the turn remains active; the broker and its tombstones are discarded at the terminal event. It is not transparently retry-safe because duplicates do not return the original success response. A duplicate while the turn is active answers 409 `tool_already_resolved`, a late output after the timeout answers 409 `tool_timed_out`; after the terminal event the same `call_id` answers 404, as does an unknown `call_id` or one belonging to a different chat, without leaking existence. Success answers 204 No Content and echoes `agent.tool.result` on the stream.

409.description: The tool call is already resolved or timed out

error.message: Tool call already resolved.

post.description: Resolves a pending `approval.request` with the user's decision. Not implemented: the endpoint is a stub and answers 409 until approval resolution is supported.

409.description: Not implemented, approval resolution is unavailable

error.message: Approval resolution is not implemented.

post.description: Copies the conversation context of the source chat into a destination chat created beforehand through the control plane. The gateway validates that the destination chat exists, belongs to the same workspace and user and carries no history and no active turn; violations answer 422. The request is rejected with 409 when a turn is in progress for the source chat. After a successful fork the two chats evolve independently.

409.description: A turn is in progress for this chat

error.message: A turn is in progress for this chat.
The destination chat is not valid for forking.

post.summary: Restore a chat from client held context
post.description: Rebuilds the orchestrator from the `orchestrator_context` supplied in the body: the compacted context first, followed by orchestrator assistant messages. Restore is the client driven rehydration path; the gateway can hydrate chats automatically from persisted context when it is available and readable. Loading is fail-open on DB/JSON errors and persistence is asynchronous best-effort, so the restored in-memory context is not a durability acknowledgement. The request is rejected with 409 when a turn is in progress for the chat and with 404 when the chat does not exist. Restore replaces the in-memory context, schedules persistence and does not open a turn, so `turn_id` answers null.

200.description: Chat restored from the supplied context

409.description: A turn is already in progress for this chat

error.message: A turn is already in progress for this chat.
The orchestrator context is not valid.

get.description: Returns protocol metadata and positively advertised names. The current alpha response is not exhaustive and a feature name may advertise an endpoint/event surface without proving the full intended semantics. The delegated_job_lifecycle feature explicitly guarantees the documented cross-team job boundary, cohort synthesis and final task output semantics. Workflows relying on these semantics must require that feature in addition to cross_team_delegation. The delegation_notify_origin feature allows optional notification suppression without changing final-job results. These additive features do not change contract version 3.

X-Envai-Extensions.description: Present only when native-tasks-v1 was accepted

get.description: Returns the current status of the API including timestamp and environment info

Public endpoint serving the JSON Web Key Set of the control plane. It publishes every Ed25519 signing key, active and retired, with its `kid` (`sig_<ulid>`), so tokens signed before a rotation keep verifying. No authentication.

post.description: Creates a workspace with id `wsp_<ulid>` owned by the authenticated user. The workspace owns the wiki, skills and `MEMORY.md` state and does not own a team. Teams are selected per chat at chat creation.

get.description: Lists the workspaces owned by the authenticated user.

200.description: Workspaces owned by the authenticated user

put.description: Updates the workspace configuration. The workspace does not own a team, so no team field is accepted here. The team is selected at chat creation through `team_id`.

post.description: Registers a user-scoped client tool with id `twl_<ulid>`. The tool is shared across all the caller's workspaces and becomes visible to an agent only when its name is in `agent_definitions.external_tools_enabled` and it is registered by the same user on the platform. `name` must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,254}$`, must be unique per user and must not be a reserved platform tool name (`read`, `list`, `stat`, `write`, `execute`, `wiki_read`, `wiki_ls`, `wiki_write`, `skill_read`, `skill_list`, `skill_write`, `exa_search`, `exa_contents`, `calculator`, `convert_units`, `delegate_task`, `set_chat_title`). `set_chat_title` is a built-in `server` tool available only to the orchestrator, never a `client` tool. `parameters` must be a JSON Schema with root type `object`; `timeout_seconds` defaults to 120 and is capped at 600.

get.description: Lists the client tools registered by the caller.

200.description: Client tools registered by the user

get.description: Returns a client tool registered by the caller, by name.

put.description: Updates a client tool. Only `description`, `parameters` and `timeout_seconds` are updatable; `name`, `kind`, `workspace_id` and `user_id` are prohibited.

delete.description: Removes the client tool from the user's registry.

post.summary: Create a chat inside a workspace
post.description: Creates a chat with id `cht_<ulid>` inside the workspace. The chat selects the team through a mandatory `team_id`. `chats.team_id` is a required 31-character `team_<ulid>` reference with a foreign key to `teams`; chat creation validates that the team exists and belongs to the chat owner, 422 otherwise. Omitting `team_id` is rejected with 422.

get.summary: List completion metadata of a chat
get.description:
Lists the metadata-only completion records of a chat, newest first. Results are paginated with `per_page` (default 15, maximum 100) and can be filtered by `status`, `model_orchestrator` and the `started_at` range (`from` and `to`, inclusive, ISO 8601). Records never include message content.
 Omitted or explicit2 selector reads the truthful numeric legacy representation; any unrepresentable item rejects the entire selected page with426. Contract3 exposes nullable current costs and immutable terminal metadata.

Returns the metadata-only record of a single completion of the chat. Omitted or explicit2 selector reads the truthful numeric legacy representation; any unrepresentable item rejects the entire selected page with426. Contract3 exposes nullable current costs and immutable terminal metadata.

get.summary: Read a workspace file or directory
get.description: Reads a single workspace file or directory through the fake filesystem api. Files answer the descriptor plus `content`, directories answer the descriptor plus alphabetically sorted `entries` (at most 500). The root `/` is allowed only here and lists the top level entries (`MEMORY.md`, `wiki`, `skills`). A missing file answers 404 with type `file_not_found`; a missing workspace answers 404 with type `not_found`.

post.description: Creates a file at the given absolute workspace-relative path, creating missing parent directories. The response is the 201 descriptor without `content`. An existing file or directory at the path answers 409 with type `file_conflict`. Content must be non empty, valid UTF-8, at most 1048576 bytes and at most 1000 lines; `/MEMORY.md` is additionally capped at 12000 characters. The root `/` and the protected `/wiki` and `/skills` paths are accepted as existing directories only, so create answers 409 for them. A missing workspace answers 404 with type `not_found`.

put.description: Overwrites the content of an existing file. The response is the 200 descriptor without `content`. A missing file answers 404 with type `file_not_found`; targeting a directory answers 409 with type `file_conflict`. Content validation matches create: non empty, valid UTF-8, at most 1048576 bytes and 1000 lines, and 12000 characters for `/MEMORY.md`. A missing workspace answers 404 with type `not_found`.

delete.summary: Delete a workspace file or directory
delete.description: Deletes a file or directory. `recursive=true` deletes a non empty directory, the default is false. The filesystem root and the protected `/wiki` and `/skills` directories cannot be deleted and answer 409 with type `file_conflict`. A missing path answers 404 with type `file_not_found`. A missing workspace answers 404 with type `not_found`.

get.description: Downloads the raw bytes of a file as an attachment. The content type comes from the extension map (markdown, text, pdf, json, csv, html, xml, yaml, image and archive types) with `application/octet-stream` as fallback; `text/*` types get `charset=utf-8` appended by the framework. Targeting a directory answers 409 with type `file_conflict`; a file too large to read answers 422 with type `file_too_large`; a malformed service response answers 422 with type `file_service_error`. Errors answer the standard JSON envelope.

Content-Disposition.description: Always `attachment` with the sanitized file name

post.summary: Convert a markdown or text file to PDF
post.description: Converts a `.md`, `.markdown` or `.txt` file to PDF and returns the document as an attachment. The conversion itself executes inside the fake filesystem service (pandoc/typst sidecar); authentication, ownership and the per-route throttle remain on this api. Other extensions are rejected with 422 before conversion. A missing file answers 404 with type `file_not_found`; a directory answers 409 with type `file_conflict`; a pdf larger than the configured cap answers 422 with type `file_too_large`. When the file service is unavailable the request answers 503 with type `file_service_unavailable`. A missing workspace answers 404 with type `not_found`.

Content-Disposition.description: Always `attachment` with the base name and `.pdf` extension

post.description: Creates an agent definition with id `agt_<ulid>` owned by the authenticated user. `mode` is `primary` or `subagent`. The optional `model` must be available in the catalog, `name` must be unique among the owner's agent definitions and `config` must not contain `max_tokens` at any nesting depth. The four jsonb fields default to empty values when omitted.

get.description: Lists the agent definitions owned by the authenticated user.

200.description: Agent definitions owned by the authenticated user

put.description: Updates the agent definition with a subset of the creation fields; at least one updatable field is required and `user_id` is prohibited. Field semantics match creation, including the `max_tokens` prohibition on `config` and the catalog availability check on `model`.

delete.description: Deletes the agent definition. The request is rejected with 422 when the agent is the orchestrator of at least one team.

post.description: Creates a team with id `team_<ulid>` owned by the authenticated user. `orchestrator_id` is required and must reference a primary-mode agent owned by the caller. The optional `members` array is ordered: `position` is derived from the array order, `role` is nullable and a member cannot be the orchestrator.

get.description: Lists the teams owned by the authenticated user with their members.

200.description: Teams owned by the authenticated user

put.description: Updates the team with a subset of `name`, `description`, `orchestrator_id` and `members`; at least one updatable field is required. When `members` is present the member list is replaced wholesale, and an empty array clears all members. `user_id` and per-member `position` and `user_id` are prohibited.

delete.description: Deletes the team. A team that still has chats cannot be deleted: the request is rejected with 422 until its chats are reassigned or removed.

get.description: Returns the LLM model catalog with team entries and the platform defaults per role. LLM entries report `deprecated` and `sunset_at` and carry the informational OpenRouter metadata synchronized from the upstream catalog; models unavailable upstream and models past sunset never appear, deprecated models appear with `deprecated: true`. Team entries are the caller's teams. The response is a top-level `{object, data, defaults}` object without a data wrapper.

post.description: Creates a long lived api key for the authenticated user. The plaintext token `envai_sk_<ulid><jwt>` appears only in the 201 response and is never persisted: the control plane stores the sha256 hash of the token, the `jti` (`key_<ulid>`), the signing key `kid` (`sig_<ulid>`), nullable `expires_at` and `revoked_at`, the owner `user_id`, `name` and `scopes`. The jwt is signed with EdDSA and carries no workspace or chat claim.

get.description: Lists the api keys owned by the authenticated user with their metadata. The plaintext token is never included.

200.description: Api keys owned by the authenticated user

delete.description: Revokes the api key: the control plane sets `revoked_at` and adds the `jti` to the Redis denylist so the key stops working immediately even when the jwt has a far future expiry. The row is never deleted. The request is rejected with 403 when the key belongs to another user and with 404 when the key does not exist.

post.description: Local and testing only echo endpoint for image generation contract validation. Accepts a multipart upload of up to 4 images and echoes the received prompt, model code and file metadata. No authentication. The request is rate limited to 10 requests per minute. The request is rejected with 404 when the application environment is not `local` or `testing`, and with 422 when the payload or the `model_code` is invalid or unsupported.

Accepts a canonical JSON image generation request and returns 202 with the accepted generation record. The request is processed asynchronously: the caller tracks progress through `status_url`. Requires an authenticated api key or web session: a missing or invalid token is rejected with 401, and the route is throttled to 30 requests per minute per user (429 when exceeded). Validation follows the Laravel `GenerateRequest`: required `model`, `prompt` and `webhook_url` (public HTTPS only, no private or reserved addresses), optional input images (`input_images` list up to 10 items, or singular `input_image`), `mask_image` and `objects_image` (each requiring `input_image` and mutually exclusive with `input_images`), `resolution`, `dimensions`, `aspect_ratio`, `format`, `quality`, `model_settings` and `providers`. Model specific validation happens server side: unknown or unsupported models, unsupported quality, resolution or aspect ratio combinations and unsafe input image URLs are rejected with 422 before provider dispatch. Upload records referenced with `upload_id` must belong to the authenticated user and be unexpired: absent, foreign, legacy (no owner) or expired records all answer the same 422 `Upload record not found.` without leaking existence. Referenced uploads are also subject to an aggregate budget of 50 MiB: the `size` of every referenced upload record is summed across all collected inputs (`input_images`, `input_image`, `mask_image` and `objects_image`) and every occurrence counts, so repeating the same `upload_id` in multiple inputs is counted multiple times. Exceeding the budget rejects the request with 422 before any record is created and before provider dispatch.

get.description: Returns the current lifecycle status of an asynchronous image generation. The `record` path segment is the generation request id `igr_<ulid>`. Requires an authenticated api key or web session: a missing or invalid token is rejected with 401. Access is scoped to the authenticated user: a record owned by another user, a legacy record without an owner or an unknown id all answer the same 404. `expires_at` is always present and is exactly two hours after creation; `submitted_at` and `completed_at` are null until the corresponding lifecycle phase happens; `result`, `error`, `files`, `price`, `usage`, `cost_usd` and `duration_ms` appear only when available.

post.description: Uploads a single image for later use in a generation request through `upload_id`. Requires an authenticated api key or web session: a missing or invalid token is rejected with 401, and the route is throttled to 20 requests per minute per user (429 when exceeded). The file must be an image of type png, jpeg, webp or gif and at most 10240 kilobytes. The record is staged for two hours and binds to exactly one generation; a bound upload cannot be reused by another generation. It returns id `upl_<ulid>`. A per user disk quota applies: the summed `size` of the user's unexpired uploads cannot exceed the configurable `envai.images.upload_quota_bytes` cap (default 200 MiB), and crossing it answers 422 `The upload storage quota has been exceeded.`. When the quota lock is not available the request answers 422 `Upload temporarily unavailable, retry.`.

get.description: Returns the image model catalog grouped by canonical model. Each entry lists the providers able to serve the model, the price classes with a provider weighted average price and the model settings. Price classes are informational: `average_price` is a provider weighted average, not a guaranteed quote, and a setting applies to the providers listed in its `providers` array, not as a universal constraint. Requires an authenticated api key or web session: a missing or invalid token is rejected with 401. The catalog is not filtered by user.

Serves a generated artifact through a relative signed URL. The `generation` (`igr_<ulid>`) and `artifact` (`art_<ulid>`) query parameters are opaque identifiers covered by the signature, so tampering with either value or with the signature is rejected with 403, and the caller can never select a disk or an object path. The optional `expires` parameter is included in every temporary signed URL and never exceeds the generation deadline. An expired signature, or an unknown, expired, foreign, keyless or malformed generation, returns a generic 404. The body is the decrypted artifact with the recorded content type (png, jpeg, webp, svg or octet-stream), `Content-Disposition: attachment`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, a restrictive `Content-Security-Policy` and `Cache-Control: no-store`. No authentication.

Content-Disposition.description: Always `attachment` with the artifact file name

post.description: Receives an asynchronous image generation webhook from a provider. The `provider` path segment selects the provider and the body is a provider specific JSON object; an empty body is tolerated by the parsers. The optional `callback_token` query parameter matches the attempt callback token, with fallback to provider job and request id lookup. A webhook is processed only when it matches an active request and attempt. Unknown, unmatched, expired and late callbacks return the same generic 200 `{status: ok}` without a data wrapper and persist no row, hash or payload; matched duplicates are dropped idempotently. Every callback passes through one uniform provider webhook rate limit applied before matching. Signature headers are optional per provider: replicate uses Svix style `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature`, fal uses `X-Fal-Webhook-Request-Id`, `X-Fal-Webhook-User-Id`, `X-Fal-Webhook-Timestamp` and `X-Fal-Webhook-Signature`, and black-forest-labs uses `X-BFL-Signature`. Missing or invalid signatures answer 401 with type `provider_error`; vertex, openai, recraft and byteplus do not support webhooks and answer 405 with type `provider_error`; unknown providers answer 422. No authentication.

NativeTasksExtension.name: X-Envai-Extensions
NativeTasksExtension.description: Opt in to native task events, capabilities and model diagnostics. Native clients send on all execution requests, including messages, capabilities and every SSE request including replay. On messages this selects detached background execution; without it background children retain the parent-bound lifecycle. Case-sensitive comma-separated tokens across repeated header values are trimmed. Unknown tokens are ignored. Every ATP request passing negotiation echoes the accepted extension; contract2 never enables it. Explicit native routes add no missing-opt-in error; Vary includes this header. Without opt-in task and delivery events project to ignorable chat.extension placeholders with empty data and null agent/turn and agent.done model diagnostics omitted, preserving original sequence IDs and the canonical log. Strict model admission is independent of this stream projection.

ContractVersion.name: X-Envai-Contract-Version
ContractVersion.description: Select contract3; no fallback or implicit coercion is permitted.

LegacyContractVersion.name: X-Envai-Contract-Version
LegacyContractVersion.description: Omission selects legacy2, restricted to truthful historical reads.

error.description: Generic delivery-turn admission failure, if any.

notify_origin.description: Requires delegation_notify_origin capability. False suppresses only automatic origin result delivery and model wake. Origin task terminal events, GET status, output and result_turn_id remain available; target child cohorts and synthesis are unchanged. Omitted and explicit true are equivalent for idempotency.

strict_model.description: Requires strict_model capability. True requires the explicitly configured root orchestrator model to be available without resolver fallback before inference or tools. Unavailable or unverifiable configuration returns 422 strict_model_unavailable. Child model selection is unchanged. The effective flag participates in idempotency; omitted and false are equivalent, and changed policy returns 409.

task_id.description: Identifier of the complete delegated job, including child cohorts and synthesis turns.

turn_id.description: Initial target coordinator turn only; its terminal need not be the job outcome.

result_turn_id.description: Final coordinator turn for a cross-team job, when available; distinct from receipt turn_id.

delivery_error.description: Native notification failure; the original task output is unchanged.

task_context.description: Complete task context, any non-null JSON value.

CompletionTerminalSnapshot.description: Immutable metadata-only terminal journal snapshot. Not a replayable ATP envelope and contains no response text. Missing/null for legacy turns. Late provider-cost reconciliation changes current completion usage_cost only.

message.description: Sanitized constant diagnostic; never assistant response text.

chat_cost.description: Frozen chat lifetime USD cost, mirroring chat_usage.cost_usd; null when incomplete or unknown.

v.description: Original immutable terminal wire version; absent only on pre-version journal records.

accepted_protocol_version.description: Version accepted before provider work. A recovered unknown-cost legacy turn can emit a v3 failure without rewriting its original acceptance.

CompletionTerminalSnapshotChatUsage.description: Chat lifetime usage frozen with this terminal snapshot; the ATP Usage fields and nullable legacy USD cost. Omitted by older recovery snapshots.

cost_usd.description: Legacy provider USD cost; null when unknown. Authoritative usage_cost preserves per-currency decimal totals and provenance; no billing.

duration_ms.description: Wall clock duration of the work in milliseconds.

sprite_ms.description: Time spent in the ephemeral Sprite sandbox, 0 when no code tool ran.

sprite_ram_gb_ms.description: Sprite RAM billed in GB-milliseconds, 0 when no code tool ran.

tool_calls.description: Tool invocations counted in the usage window.

error_code.description: Sanitized stable conversion failure code; never a raw provider response or secret. Null when no failure is recorded.

recoverable.description: True only when an automatic technical recovery is durably scheduled and eligible: attempts remain and the source has not completed or been withdrawn. False for initial queued work, healthy running, terminal failures and exhausted retries.

next_retry_at.description: Time of the scheduled automatic technical recovery when recoverable is true; otherwise null. Not an initial work schedule or an operator-repair promise.

message.description: A free-form explanation reported by the managed inbox, not a verified provider fact.

Error.description: Standard error envelope shared by both planes

code.description: Optional machine-readable error code, for example `turn_in_progress`, `no_turn_in_progress` or `invalid_fork_destination`. Null when not applicable.

details.description: Additional error details (for example validation errors)

mime_type.description: Original MIME type for native originals; omitted on legacy converted manifests.

mode.description: Native original delivery marker; omitted on legacy converted manifests.

error_code.description: Sanitized stable conversion failure code; never a raw provider response or secret. Null when no failure is recorded.

recoverable.description: True only when an automatic technical recovery is durably scheduled and eligible: attempts remain and the source has not completed or been withdrawn. False for initial queued work, healthy running, terminal failures and exhausted retries.

next_retry_at.description: Time of the scheduled automatic technical recovery when recoverable is true; otherwise null. Not an initial work schedule or an operator-repair promise.

retryable.description: Explicit retry is permitted; uncertain provider outcomes cannot be resubmitted.

file.description: Native original; MD TXT CSV PDF MP3 MP4 only. The configured per-file native byte limit applies and no conversion, OCR or transcription is scheduled.

ChatMessageRequest.description: User text and IDs of ready native original attachments from this chat. Requires chat_attachments capability and Idempotency-Key when IDs are supplied. Native originals are delivered to compatible models as private content parts; no conversion, OCR or transcription is requested and no file is silently omitted.

message.description: User message, becomes the turn input
message.example: Summarize the last week of traffic

attachment_ids.description: Ordered attachment IDs. The acceptance acknowledgment returns these IDs in the same order.

strict_model.description: Requires strict_model capability. True requires the explicitly configured root orchestrator model to be available without resolver fallback before inference or tools. Unavailable or unverifiable configuration returns 422 strict_model_unavailable. Child model selection is unchanged. The effective flag participates in idempotency; omitted and false are equivalent, and changed policy returns 409.

ChatMessageAccepted.description: Acknowledgment for an accepted message. The message opened a turn identified by `turn_id` (the orchestrator completion id).

turn_id.description: Turn id `cmpl_<ulid>` of the started turn

attachment_ids.description: Ordered attachment IDs. The acceptance acknowledgment returns these IDs in the same order.

TurnAccepted.description: Acknowledgment for an accepted asynchronous chat control operation (cancel, steer). Carries the `turn_id` of the affected turn.

turn_id.description: Turn id `cmpl_<ulid>` of the affected turn

ToolOutputRequest.description: Payload to resolve a pending client tool call

output.description: Client output delivered to the resumed branch. 128 KiB limit enforced by the gateway.

is_error.description: Whether the client tool failed, default false

ApprovalRequest.description: Payload to resolve a pending approval

reason.description: User note attached to the decision
reason.example: Approved, keep the budget under 10 dollars

SteerRequest.description: Payload to record guidance for an active turn. `target_agent_id` is optional and targets the orchestrator when omitted. Current alpha emits `turn.steered` but does not inject the text into the running LLM loop.

text.example: Prefer the cheaper provider for this turn

target_agent_id.description: Running agent instance id `ag_<ulid>`, null or absent targets the orchestrator. A value that is present but does not match the agent id shape, including the explicit empty string, is rejected with 422 validation_error and no event is recorded.

ForkChatRequest.description: Payload to fork a chat. The destination chat must exist, belong to the same workspace and user and carry no history and no active turn; it is created beforehand through the control plane.

destination_chat_id.description: Chat id `cht_<ulid>` of the destination chat

ChatForked.description: Fork acknowledgement with the source and destination chats

destination_chat_id.description: Chat id `cht_<ulid>` of the destination chat

OrchestratorContextItem.description: One element of the `orchestrator_context` supplied on restore. The first element must have `kind` `compacted`, the compacted context summary; subsequent elements are `assistant` orchestrator messages emitted after the compact point.

kind.description: `compacted` is the compacted context summary and must be the first element of the context; `assistant` is an orchestrator assistant message following the compact.

turn_id.description: Turn id `cmpl_<ulid>` the assistant message belongs to, null when not applicable.

content.description: Compacted context summary or assistant message content
content.example: Ecco l'analisi del traffico: 12k visitatori, +8% rispetto alla scorsa settimana.

RestoreChatRequest.description: Payload to restore a chat from client held context. The `orchestrator_context` lists the compacted context first, followed by orchestrator assistant messages. It replaces in-memory history and schedules asynchronous best-effort persistence; the accepted response does not prove that durable storage succeeded.

orchestrator_context.description: The orchestrator context, the compacted context first followed by orchestrator assistant messages. The first element must have `kind` `compacted`.

example.content: Compattazione del contesto fino al turno cmpl_01j5abcdefghjkmnpqrstvwxyz.
Ecco l'analisi del traffico: 12k visitatori, +8% rispetto alla scorsa settimana.

RestoreChatAccepted.description: Acknowledgment for a restore request. The chat was rehydrated from the supplied orchestrator context; `turn_id` is always null because restore does not open a turn.

turn_id.description: Always null, restore does not open a turn

Capabilities.description: Event families and optional features advertised by the server. `event_types` is a positive discovery list rather than a parser allowlist, `tool_kinds` lists the supported tool kinds and `features` positively advertised protocol surfaces. A feature name does not by itself prove that every intended semantic is implemented; for example the server advertises `replay` while retention is an in-memory window. `steer` is not advertised: the endpoint records `turn.steered` but does not inject the text into the running LLM loop. Clients remain forward compatible with valid ATP events absent from this response.

families.description: Event families the negotiated surface may emit; task requires native-tasks-v1

event_types.description: Dotted event types the server actually emits; additive and not an exhaustive parser allowlist

tool_kinds.description: Tool kinds supported by the server

features.description: Optional protocol features implemented by the server. Require delegated_job_lifecycle before enabling workflows that use complete delegated-job outcomes; cross_team_delegation alone is insufficient.

Workspace.description: A workspace owns the wiki, skills and `MEMORY.md` state. It does not own a team. Teams are selected per chat through `chat.team_id`. The `user_id` property is the owner user.

WorkspaceResource.description: Laravel JsonResource wrapper for a single workspace

WorkspaceMetadata.description: Laravel metadata is stored and returned as JSON derived from a PHP array, so it can be an associative JSON object or a JSON list. The default is an empty array.

WorkspaceCreateRequest.description: Payload to create a workspace. No team field: the workspace does not own a team.

WorkspaceUpdateRequest.description: Payload to update a workspace. No team field: teams are selected per chat. At least one of `name` or `metadata` must be provided.

UserTool.description: A user-scoped client tool with id `twl_<ulid>`. The `kind` is always `client`. The tool is shared across all the caller's workspaces and is visible to an agent only when its `name` is in the agent definition `external_tools_enabled` and it is registered by the same user on the platform. Names are unique per user.

name.description: Tool name, unique per user, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,254}$`. Reserved platform tool names are rejected.

description.description: Free text description shown to the LLM, null when not set
description.example: Send an email through the client SMTP server

parameters.description: JSON Schema describing the tool arguments, shown to the LLM. The root `type` must be `object`.

timeout_seconds.description: Resolution deadline for `agent.tool.request` of this tool, default 120 seconds, max 600.

UserToolResource.description: Laravel JsonResource wrapper for a single user tool

UserToolCreateRequest.description: Payload to register a client tool for the caller's user registry. `name` and `parameters` are required; `kind` defaults to `client`; `description` is optional; `timeout_seconds` defaults to 120 (min 1, max 600). `workspace_id` and `user_id` are prohibited.

name.description: Tool name, unique per user. Reserved platform tool names, including `set_chat_title`, are rejected.

description.description: Free text description shown to the LLM
description.example: Send an email through the client SMTP server

parameters.description: JSON Schema describing the tool arguments. The root `type` must be `object`.

timeout_seconds.description: Resolution deadline in seconds, default 120, max 600

UserToolUpdateRequest.description: Payload to update a client tool in the user's registry. Only `description`, `parameters` and `timeout_seconds` are accepted; `name`, `kind`, `workspace_id` and `user_id` are prohibited. At least one field is required.

description.description: Free text description shown to the LLM

parameters.description: JSON Schema describing the tool arguments. The root `type` must be `object`.

Chat.description: A chat inside a workspace with id `cht_<ulid>`. The `team_id` selects the team for the chat. It is a required 31-character `team_<ulid>` reference with a foreign key to `teams`, validated at chat creation to exist and belong to the chat owner. The `user_id` property is the owner user.

team_id.description: Team id (conventionally `team_<ulid>`), up to 31 characters, selected at chat creation. It is a foreign key to `teams`; chat creation validates that the team exists and belongs to the chat owner, 422 otherwise.

title.description: Server/runtime-managed chat title, null before it is generated

ChatResource.description: Laravel JsonResource wrapper for a single chat

ChatCreateRequest.description: Payload to create a chat inside a workspace. The chat selects the team through a mandatory `team_id`. Chat creation validates that the team exists and belongs to the chat owner, 422 otherwise; omitting `team_id` is also 422.

team_id.description: Team id (conventionally `team_<ulid>`), up to 31 characters. It is a foreign key to `teams`; chat creation validates that the team exists and belongs to the chat owner, 422 otherwise.

Completion.description: Metadata-only record of a model turn inside a chat, with id `cmpl_<ulid>`. It never contains message content: usage, cost and lifecycle fields summarize the turn while the content lives in the execution plane stream. The `user_id` property is the owner user.

team_id.description: Team id `team_<ulid>` selected by the chat at creation

model_orchestrator.description: Model id used by the team orchestrator, or null when not yet resolved

models_subagents.description: Model ids used by the subagents of the turn

finished_at.description: Turn end timestamp in UTC, null while the turn is running

duration_ms.description: Turn duration in milliseconds, null while the turn is running

usage.description: Aggregated usage metadata of the turn

terminal_snapshot.description: Optional immutable metadata-only terminal outcome, not response-text replay. Null or absent for legacy turns; current costs can advance without changing this snapshot.

cost_usd.description: For tracked scopes, complete USD-only provider total or zero for a closed empty scope; null while pending or when a multi-currency total cannot be represented. Historical no-scope values remain unchanged. usage_cost is authoritative and never a customer charge.

content_hash.description: Optional hash of the turn content; the content itself is never stored

CompletionResource.description: Laravel JsonResource wrapper for a single completion

CompletionCollection.description: Laravel JsonResource collection wrapper for a paginated completion list

Agent.description: An agent definition with id `agt_<ulid>` owned by a user with id `usr_<ulid>`. `mode` is `primary` (usable as team orchestrator) or `subagent`. `config` must not contain `max_tokens` at any nesting depth. The `user_id` property is the owner user.

description.description: Free text description, null when not set

tools_enabled.description: Tools enabled for the agent, default empty list

external_tools_enabled.description: Tools the agent may receive from the caller, default empty list. A client tool is visible to the agent only when its name is here and it is registered by the same user on the platform (`user_tools`); no derived restrictions apply to client tools.

permissions.description: Free form permissions object, default empty object

can_write_knowledge.description: Whether the agent may write wiki knowledge, default false

can_write_skills.description: Whether the agent may write skills, default false

AgentCreateRequest.description: Payload to create an agent definition. `name`, `system_prompt` and `mode` are required; `user_id` is prohibited. `description` and `model` are optional and `model` must be available in the catalog when provided. The four jsonb fields default to empty values when omitted.

model.description: Model id of the catalog. When provided it must be available (not removed or past sunset), otherwise the request is rejected with 422.

tools_enabled.description: Tools enabled for the agent, default empty list

external_tools_enabled.description: Tools the agent may receive from the caller, default empty list. A client tool is visible to the agent only when its name is here and it is registered by the same user on the platform (`user_tools`).

permissions.description: Free form permissions object, default empty object

can_write_knowledge.description: Whether the agent may write wiki knowledge, default false

can_write_skills.description: Whether the agent may write skills, default false

config.description: Free form agent configuration, default empty object. Must not contain `max_tokens` at any nesting depth.

AgentUpdateRequest.description: Payload to update an agent definition. Any subset of the creation fields is accepted and at least one updatable field is required; `user_id` is prohibited. Field semantics match creation.

model.description: Model id of the catalog. When provided it must be available (not removed or past sunset), otherwise the request is rejected with 422.

tools_enabled.description: Tools enabled for the agent, default empty list

external_tools_enabled.description: Tools the agent may receive from the caller, default empty list. A client tool is visible to the agent only when its name is here and it is registered by the same user on the platform (`user_tools`).

permissions.description: Free form permissions object, default empty object

can_write_knowledge.description: Whether the agent may write wiki knowledge, default false

can_write_skills.description: Whether the agent may write skills, default false

config.description: Free form agent configuration, default empty object. Must not contain `max_tokens` at any nesting depth.

AgentTool.description: Tool reference of `tools_enabled` or `external_tools_enabled`. The `name` is required; additional keys are allowed. For `external_tools_enabled`, `name` matches a client tool registered by the same user on the platform (`user_tools`).

Team.description: A team with id `team_<ulid>` owned by a user with id `usr_<ulid>`. It has exactly one orchestrator, a primary-mode agent owned by the same user, and an ordered member list. The `user_id` property is the owner user.

description.description: Free text description, null when not set

orchestrator_id.description: Agent definition id `agt_<ulid>`, 30 characters, of the primary-mode orchestrator agent owned by the same user

TeamResource.description: Laravel JsonResource wrapper for a single team

TeamCreateRequest.description: Payload to create a team. `name` and `orchestrator_id` are required; `orchestrator_id` must reference a primary-mode agent owned by the caller. `members` is optional and ordered: `position` is derived from the array order. `user_id` and per-member `position` and `user_id` are prohibited.

orchestrator_id.description: Agent definition id `agt_<ulid>`, 30 characters. Must reference a primary-mode agent owned by the caller, otherwise the request is rejected with 422.

members.description: Ordered member list; `position` is derived from the array order. Empty when absent.

TeamUpdateRequest.description: Payload to update a team. Any subset of `name`, `description`, `orchestrator_id` and `members` is accepted and at least one updatable field is required. When `members` is present the member list is replaced wholesale, and an empty array clears all members. `user_id` and per-member `position` and `user_id` are prohibited.

orchestrator_id.description: Agent definition id `agt_<ulid>`, 30 characters. Must reference a primary-mode agent owned by the caller, otherwise the request is rejected with 422. When the orchestrator changes without `members`, it must not be an existing member.

members.description: Ordered member list; `position` is derived from the array order. When present the previous member list is replaced; an empty array clears all members.

TeamMember.description: Team member record with the resolved agent name and the pivot position and role.

name.description: Name of the member agent definition

position.description: Member position in the team, derived from the request array order

role.description: Team scoped role label, null when not set

TeamMemberCreateRequest.description: Member reference accepted in team create and update payloads. `agent_definition_id` must reference an agent definition owned by the caller, must be distinct from the other members and cannot be the orchestrator. `position` is derived from the array order and is prohibited here; `user_id` is prohibited.

role.description: Team scoped role label, null when not set

ApiKey.description: Api key metadata. The plaintext token is never included: it appears only in the 201 creation response.

id.description: Api key id `key_<ulid>`, 30 characters, the jwt `jti`

scopes.description: Capability scopes of the key, default `["completions:write"]`

expires_at.description: Expiration timestamp, null when the key never expires. The jwt omits `exp` in that case and stays valid until revocation.

revoked_at.description: Revocation timestamp, null while the key is active

ApiKeyCreated.description: Laravel JsonResource wrapper for a created api key

data.description: Api key metadata plus the plaintext token shown once

ApiKeyCollection.description: Laravel JsonResource collection wrapper for api keys

data.description: Api key metadata without the token

ApiKeyCreate.description: Payload to create an api key. `user_id` is prohibited: the owner is the authenticated user. `scopes` defaults to `["completions:write"]` and `expires_at` defaults to `30d`.

scopes.description: Capability scopes of the key, default `["completions:write"]`

expires_at.description: Expiration window, default `30d`. `never` creates a key without expiry that stays valid until revocation.

JwksDocument.description: JSON Web Key Set of the control plane signing keys

keys.description: Every signing key, active and retired

Jwk.description: Ed25519 public signing key entry. `kid` is the signing key id `sig_<ulid>`; retired keys stay published so tokens signed before the rotation keep verifying.

ModelList.description: Top-level model catalog response without a data wrapper: `object` is always `list`, `data` mixes LLM entries and team alias entries and `defaults` carries the platform default model id per role.

ModelListEntry.description: Single catalog entry, either an LLM or a team alias

LlmModelEntry.description: LLM entry of the catalog. `owned_by` is the model provider. Models that are unavailable upstream or past sunset are removed from the catalog and never appear; deprecated models appear with `deprecated: true` until sunset. The OpenRouter metadata fields are informational copies of the upstream catalog: `pricing` never drives billing, which uses the provider `usage.cost`.

created.description: Unix timestamp of the model release date

deprecated.description: Whether the model is in the deprecation period before sunset

sunset_at.description: ISO 8601 sunset date, null when the model is never removed

display_name.description: Human readable model name from the upstream catalog

description.description: Model description from the upstream catalog

canonical_slug.description: Permanent upstream slug for the model

hugging_face_id.description: Hugging Face model id when the upstream catalog publishes one

context_length.description: Maximum context window size in tokens

max_completion_tokens.description: Maximum completion tokens reported by the top provider

supported_parameters.description: Parameter names accepted by the model

default_parameters.description: Default parameter values published by the upstream catalog

reasoning.description: Reasoning capabilities published by the upstream catalog

knowledge_cutoff.description: Knowledge cutoff date published by the upstream catalog

upstream_expiration_date.description: Upstream deprecation date. It is informational and never sets the local `sunset_at` lifecycle field.

is_moderated.description: Whether the top provider moderates the model

synced_at.description: When the entry was last synchronized from the upstream catalog

OpenRouterPricing.description: Informational pricing copied verbatim from the upstream catalog. Values are exact decimal strings and are never converted to floats; nested provider overrides are preserved as published. Billing uses the provider `usage.cost`, not this object.

OpenRouterArchitecture.description: Technical capabilities published by the upstream catalog

OpenRouterAliasTarget.description: Alias target published by the upstream catalog for router models

TeamModelEntry.description: Team entry of the catalog. `team_id` is the team key. `deprecated` is always false and `sunset_at` is always null.

created.description: Unix timestamp of the team creation

ModelDefaults.description: Platform default model id per role, used at runtime when no model is configured.

orchestrator.description: Default model id for the orchestrator role

subagent.description: Default model id for the subagent role

TestImageGenerateRequest.description: Multipart payload for `POST /tests/images/generate`. Sends up to 4 image files together with the prompt and the model code. The files array must contain at least one image and each file must be a valid image of at most 10240 kilobytes.

files.description: Image files to echo back, 1 to 4 items, each at most 10240 KB

prompt.example: A beautiful sunset over the mountains

model_code.description: Model code echoed back unchanged. When present it must be known to the provider registry, otherwise the request is rejected with 422.

TestImageFileMetadata.description: Metadata of a single uploaded file

TestImageGenerateResource.description: Laravel JsonResource wrapper for the test generation echo

prompt.example: A beautiful sunset over the mountains

InputImage.description: Input image reference used by `input_images`, `input_image`, `mask_image` and `objects_image`. The `type` selects how `payload` must be interpreted: `url` (public http or https URL, private and reserved addresses rejected), `base64` (raw or data URI prefixed base64 of a png, jpeg or webp image, at most 10485760 characters) or `upload_id` (id of an existing, unexpired image upload record).

payload.description: URL, base64 image data or upload record id depending on `type`. Max length 10485760 characters.

reference.description: Optional client reference for the image

mime_type.description: Declared image mime type; null when not declared

ImageGenerationRequest.description: Canonical JSON payload for `POST /images/generations`. Mutual exclusions are enforced: `input_image` and `input_images` are mutually exclusive, `mask_image` and `objects_image` require `input_image` and cannot be combined with `input_images`. Unknown top level fields are rejected with 422. Upload records referenced with `upload_id` count against an aggregate budget of 50 MiB summed across all inputs, one occurrence at a time; exceeding the budget is rejected with 422 before record creation and provider dispatch.

model.description: Canonical model code, for example `google/nano-banana-2`, `flux/flux-2-max` or `openai/gpt-image-1.5`. Unknown or unsupported models are rejected with 422 before provider dispatch.

prompt.example: A beautiful sunset over the mountains

webhook_url.description: Public HTTPS callback URL, at most 2048 characters. Private, reserved, loopback or metadata addresses are rejected.

input_images.description: List of input images, at most 10 items. Mutually exclusive with `input_image`, `mask_image` and `objects_image`.

quality.description: Output quality between 1 and 100; model dependent support

ImageUploadRecord.description: Uploaded input image record staged for two hours and bindable to one generation

ImageUploadResource.description: Laravel JsonResource wrapper for an uploaded image

ImageUploadRequest.description: Multipart payload for `POST /images/uploads`. A single image file of type png, jpeg, webp or gif, at most 10240 kilobytes.

ModelCatalogEntry.description: Canonical model entry of the image model catalog

providers.description: Providers able to serve the model

model_settings.description: Model settings exposed by the providers

ModelSetting.description: Model setting exposed by one or more providers. The setting applies to the providers listed in `providers` only; it is not a universal constraint for the model.

enum.description: Allowed values when the setting is an enum

range.description: Inclusive minimum and maximum when the setting is numeric

defaults_by_provider.description: Per provider default values when they differ

ModelCatalogResource.description: Laravel JsonResource collection wrapper for the model catalog

ProviderWebhookPayload.description: Provider specific webhook body. The shape depends on the provider; common fields are the provider job or request id and the lifecycle status. Unknown fields are tolerated by the provider parsers.

WorkspaceFile.description: Workspace file or directory representation returned inside the `{data: ...}` wrapper. The first six fields form the descriptor; `content` is added for files and `entries` for directories by the resource. Create and update responses return the descriptor only.

path.description: Workspace-relative path without the leading slash, for example `wiki/guide.md` or `wiki`

name.description: Base name of the file or directory

size.description: Size in bytes as reported by the file service

modified_at.description: Last modification timestamp, null when not reported

mime_type.description: Mime type of a file, always null for directories

content.description: File content, present only when the target is a file

entries.description: Child descriptors, present only when the target is a directory

WorkspaceFileEntry.description: Descriptor of a single child of a directory listing

path.description: Workspace-relative path without the leading slash, for example `wiki/alpha.md` or `wiki/sub`

size.description: Size in bytes as reported by the file service

modified_at.description: Last modification timestamp, null when not reported

mime_type.description: Mime type of a file, always null for directories

WorkspaceFileResource.description: Laravel JsonResource wrapper for a workspace file or directory

WorkspaceFileRequest.description: Shared payload of create and update. `path` is an absolute workspace-relative path, `content` is the file body. Content must be non empty, valid UTF-8, at most 1048576 bytes and at most 1000 lines; writing `/MEMORY.md` additionally caps the content at 12000 characters.

path.description: Absolute workspace-relative path, for example `/wiki/guide.md` or `/MEMORY.md`. Must start with a slash and must not contain `..`, backslashes, control characters, duplicate or trailing slashes.

content.description: File content, non empty, at most 1048576 bytes and 1000 lines

ConvertToPdfRequest.description: Payload of `POST /files/convert-to-pdf`. The `path` must reference a markdown or text file: the extension must be `.md`, `.markdown` or `.txt`, otherwise the request is rejected with 422.

path.description: Absolute workspace-relative path of a `.md`, `.markdown` or `.txt` file

ThrottleError.description: Laravel throttle response using the standard error envelope

CapabilitiesLegacy.description: Event families and optional features advertised by the server. `event_types` is a positive discovery list rather than a parser allowlist, `tool_kinds` lists the supported tool kinds and `features` positively advertised protocol surfaces. A feature name does not by itself prove that every intended semantic is implemented; for example the server advertises `replay` while retention is an in-memory window. `steer` is not advertised: the endpoint records `turn.steered` but does not inject the text into the running LLM loop. Clients remain forward compatible with valid ATP events absent from this response.

families.description: Event families the server may emit

event_types.description: Dotted event types the server actually emits; additive and not an exhaustive parser allowlist

tool_kinds.description: Tool kinds supported by the server

features.description: Optional protocol features implemented by the server
